title: Clinical Performance Evaluation of Intelligenome CRISPR-TB Blood Test
summary:
Tuberculosis (TB) is a serious infectious disease that can be hard to diagnose quickly and accurately. Many people with TB are not diagnosed in time, which contributes to a high number of deaths worldwide. Current tests like the GeneXpert system, while recommended by the World Health Organization, have limitations—especially when TB occurs outside the lungs.
This study is testing a new blood test, called the CRISPR-TB Blood Test, which uses advanced CRISPR technology to detect traces of TB bacteria in a patient’s blood. Unlike older tests that often require a sample of sputum (mucus from the lungs), this test only needs a simple blood sample, making it easier and potentially faster.
The study will compare this new test’s accuracy to existing standard tests (like GeneXpert and lab cultures) in diagnosing active TB disease. It will be carried out in hospitals and clinics in the US, Mexico, and Europe, enrolling adults who might have TB. The goal is to show that this blood test works just as well—or even better—than current methods, and that it can help doctors diagnose TB more quickly, especially in settings with fewer resources.

interventions.name: Testing of blood samples for Mtb infection with the investigational device.
Testing of sputum samples (from the same group) for Mtb infection with the comparator device.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Agree with the content and able to sign the Informed Consent Form.
Has clinical signs and symptoms typically associated with active TB disease.
Exclusion criteria:
Has medical emergency
Pregnancy
Insufficient physical or mental health condition
Having TB treatment for longer than 3 days before enrollment
Impaired cognitive function
